name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATION_COMPOUNDS_MATCH_Q01 - Moles of silver chloride precipitated per mole

questiontext.text:
Match the coordination compounds given in Column I with the moles of \(\mathrm{AgCl}\) precipitated per mole of compound on reaction with excess silver nitrate solution given in Column II:

Column IColumn II
A. \(\mathrm{CoCl_{3}\cdot 6NH_{3}}\)i. \(0\text{ mol}\)
B. \(\mathrm{CoCl_{3}\cdot 5NH_{3}}\)ii. \(1\text{ mol}\)
C. \(\mathrm{CoCl_{3}\cdot 4NH_{3}}\)iii. \(2\text{ mol}\)
D. \(\mathrm{CoCl_{3}\cdot 3NH_{3}}\)iv. \(3\text{ mol}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Werner's formulation of coordination compounds
According to Werner's theory, the groups inside the coordination sphere (enclosed in square brackets) are non-ionisable and bonded by secondary valencies, while groups outside the coordination sphere satisfy primary valencies and ionise in aqueous solution to yield chloride ions that precipitate as \(\mathrm{AgCl}\) on treatment with excess cold \(\mathrm{AgNO_{3}}\) solution.

Step 2: Analysis of the hexammine complex
The complex \(\mathrm{CoCl_{3}\cdot 6NH_{3}}\) is formulated as \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_{3})_{6}]Cl_{3}}\). In aqueous solution, one mole of this complex dissociates into three moles of chloride ions, precipitating \(3\text{ mol}\) of \(\mathrm{AgCl}\).

Step 3: Analysis of the pentammine complex
The complex \(\mathrm{CoCl_{3}\cdot 5NH_{3}}\) is formulated as \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_{3})_{5}Cl]Cl_{2}}\). It possesses two ionisable chloride ions outside the coordination sphere, precipitating \(2\text{ mol}\) of \(\mathrm{AgCl}\).

Step 4: Analysis of the tetrammine complex
The complex \(\mathrm{CoCl_{3}\cdot 4NH_{3}}\) is formulated as \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_{3})_{4}Cl_{2}]Cl}\). It has one ionisable chloride ion outside the coordination sphere, yielding \(1\text{ mol}\) of \(\mathrm{AgCl}\).

Step 5: Analysis of the triammine complex
The complex \(\mathrm{CoCl_{3}\cdot 3NH_{3}}\) is formulated as \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_{3})_{3}Cl_{3}]}\). All three chloride ions reside inside the coordination sphere satisfying secondary valencies; hence no chloride ions ionise in solution, resulting in \(0\text{ mol}\) of \(\mathrm{AgCl}\).

Step 6: Final Conclusion
The correct correspondence is: \(\mathrm{CoCl_{3}\cdot 6NH_{3}}\) pairs with \(3\text{ mol}\), \(\mathrm{CoCl_{3}\cdot 5NH_{3}}\) pairs with \(2\text{ mol}\), \(\mathrm{CoCl_{3}\cdot 4NH_{3}}\) pairs with \(1\text{ mol}\), and \(\mathrm{CoCl_{3}\cdot 3NH_{3}}\) pairs with \(0\text{ mol}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATION_COMPOUNDS_MATCH_Q02 - Coordination polyhedra of common complex entities

questiontext.text:
Match the coordination entities in Column I with their respective coordination polyhedra (geometrical arrangements) in Column II:

Column IColumn II
A. \(\mathrm{[Ni(CO)_{4}]}\)i. Octahedral
B. \(\mathrm{[PtCl_{4}]^{2-}}\)ii. Trigonal bipyramidal
C. \(\mathrm{[Fe(CO)_{5}]}\)iii. Tetrahedral
D. \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_{3})_{6}]^{3+}}\)iv. Square planar

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual definition of coordination polyhedron
The spatial arrangement of the ligand atoms directly attached to the central metal atom or ion defines a coordination polyhedron about the central metal.

Step 2: Geometry of tetracarbonylnickel(0)
Nickel in \(\mathrm{[Ni(CO)_{4}]}\) has an oxidation state of zero with electronic configuration \(3d^{10}\). The metal centre undergoes \(sp^3\) hybridisation, giving a tetrahedral coordination polyhedron.

Step 3: Geometry of tetrachloridoplatinate(II)
Platinum(II) in \(\mathrm{[PtCl_{4}]^{2-}}\) is a \(5d^8\) system. Square planar geometry is strongly favoured for \(4d\) and \(5d\) metal ions with \(d^8\) configurations involving \(dsp^2\) hybridisation.

Step 4: Geometry of pentacarbonyliron(0)
Iron in \(\mathrm{[Fe(CO)_{5}]}\) has zero oxidation state and coordination number 5. Pairing of \(3d\) electrons provides one empty inner \(d\) orbital, leading to \(dsp^3\) hybridisation with a trigonal bipyramidal coordination polyhedron.

Step 5: Geometry of hexaamminecobalt(III)
Cobalt(III) in \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_{3})_{6}]^{3+}}\) has coordination number 6. Six ligand donor atoms surround the cobalt ion symmetrically at the vertices of an octahedron, yielding an octahedral coordination polyhedron.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
The correct correspondence is: \(\mathrm{[Ni(CO)_{4}]}\) corresponds to tetrahedral, \(\mathrm{[PtCl_{4}]^{2-}}\) corresponds to square planar, \(\mathrm{[Fe(CO)_{5}]}\) corresponds to trigonal bipyramidal, and \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_{3})_{6}]^{3+}}\) corresponds to octahedral.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATION_COMPOUNDS_MATCH_Q03 - Biological and medicinal coordination compounds and metals

questiontext.text:
Match the biological/medicinal coordination compounds in Column I with the central metal atom/ion present in them in Column II:

Column IColumn II
A. Chlorophylli. Cobalt
B. Haemoglobinii. Platinum
C. Vitamin \(\mathrm{B_{12}}\)iii. Magnesium
D. Cis-platiniv. Iron

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Bio-inorganic roles of coordination complexes
Coordination compounds are vital components of biological systems and have profound applications in medicine. Specific metal ions serve as the active coordination centers in complex biomolecules and pharmaceuticals.

Step 2: Identification of metal in chlorophyll
Chlorophyll is the green pigment in plants responsible for photosynthesis; it is a coordination compound containing magnesium as its central metal.

Step 3: Identification of metal in haemoglobin
Haemoglobin is the red pigment in erythrocytes responsible for oxygen transport; it is a coordination compound containing iron(II) coordinated to a porphyrin ring.

Step 4: Identification of metal in vitamin B12
Vitamin \(\mathrm{B_{12}}\) (cyanocobalamin), which prevents pernicious anaemia, is a macrocyclic corrin ring coordination complex of cobalt.

Step 5: Identification of metal in cis-platin
Cis-platin, \(\mathrm{\textit{cis}\text{-}[Pt(NH_{3})_{2}Cl_{2}]}\), is an established anti-tumour platinum complex used in cancer chemotherapy.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
The correct correspondence is: Chlorophyll pairs with Magnesium, Haemoglobin pairs with Iron, Vitamin \(\mathrm{B_{12}}\) pairs with Cobalt, and Cis-platin pairs with Platinum.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATION_COMPOUNDS_MATCH_Q04 - Types of structural isomerism in complex pairs

questiontext.text:
Match the pairs of coordination compounds in Column I with the type of isomerism they exhibit in Column II:

Column IColumn II
A. \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_{3})_{5}(NO_{2})]Cl_{2}}\) and \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_{3})_{5}(ONO)]Cl_{2}}\)i. Coordination isomerism
B. \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_{3})_{6}][Cr(CN)_{6}]}\) and \(\mathrm{[Cr(NH_{3})_{6}][Co(CN)_{6}]}\)ii. Solvate (hydrate) isomerism
C. \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_{3})_{5}(SO_{4})]Br}\) and \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_{3})_{5}Br]SO_{4}}\)iii. Linkage isomerism
D. \(\mathrm{[Cr(H_{2}O)_{6}]Cl_{3}}\) and \(\mathrm{[Cr(H_{2}O)_{5}Cl]Cl_{2}\cdot H_{2}O}\)iv. Ionisation isomerism

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Principles of structural isomerism
Structural isomers have the same empirical formula but differ in the arrangement of chemical bonds, distribution of ligands between spheres, or ligand binding mode.

Step 2: Linkage isomerism
Linkage isomerism arises in a coordination compound containing an ambidentate ligand capable of coordinating through two different donor atoms. In \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_{3})_{5}(NO_{2})]Cl_{2}}\), the nitrite ligand binds through nitrogen, whereas in \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_{3})_{5}(ONO)]Cl_{2}}\), it binds through oxygen. This represents linkage isomerism.

Step 3: Coordination isomerism
Coordination isomerism occurs in compounds composed of both complex cation and complex anion due to the interchange of ligands between the two metal entities. \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_{3})_{6}][Cr(CN)_{6}]}\) and \(\mathrm{[Cr(NH_{3})_{6}][Co(CN)_{6}]}\) illustrate coordination isomerism.

Step 4: Ionisation isomerism
Ionisation isomerism arises when a counter ion in a compound displaces a ligand from the coordination sphere, producing different ions in solution. \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_{3})_{5}(SO_{4})]Br}\) gives bromide ions while \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_{3})_{5}Br]SO_{4}}\) gives sulphate ions upon dissociation in water. This represents ionisation isomerism.

Step 5: Solvate isomerism
Solvate (hydrate) isomerism differs by whether a solvent molecule (water) is directly bonded to the metal ion as a ligand or merely present as free solvent molecules of crystallisation in the crystal lattice. \(\mathrm{[Cr(H_{2}O)_{6}]Cl_{3}}\) and \(\mathrm{[Cr(H_{2}O)_{5}Cl]Cl_{2}\cdot H_{2}O}\) illustrate solvate isomerism.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
The correct correspondence is: the pair with nitro and nitrito complexes matches linkage isomerism; the hexammine-hexacyanide complex pair matches coordination isomerism; the sulphato-bromido complex pair matches ionisation isomerism; and the hydrated chromium chloride pair matches solvate isomerism.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATION_COMPOUNDS_MATCH_Q05 - Classification and denticity of various ligands

questiontext.text:
Match the ligands given in Column I with their denticity/bonding character described in Column II:

Column IColumn II
A. \(\mathrm{EDTA^{4-}}\)i. Ambidentate unidentate ligand
B. Ethane-1,2-diamineii. Neutral unidentate ligand
C. \(\mathrm{SCN^{-}}\)iii. Hexadentate chelating ligand
D. \(\mathrm{NH_{3}}\)iv. Didentate chelating ligand

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Principles of ligand denticity
The number of donor atoms through which a ligand binds to a single central metal ion is known as its denticity. Ligands binding through two or more donor sites are polydentate (chelating), whereas those coordinating through one site are unidentate.

Step 2: Denticity of ethylenediaminetetraacetate
Ethylenediaminetetraacetate ion (\(\mathrm{EDTA^{4-}}\)) possesses two nitrogen donor atoms and four oxygen donor atoms from acetate groups, allowing it to bind through six donor atoms simultaneously as an important hexadentate chelating ligand.

Step 3: Denticity of ethane-1,2-diamine
Ethane-1,2-diamine (\(\mathrm{H_{2}NCH_{2}CH_{2}NH_{2}}\)) has two nitrogen donor atoms each bearing a lone pair of electrons. It binds via two donor atoms to form a stable ring structure, acting as a didentate chelating ligand.

Step 4: Bonding mode of thiocyanate
Thiocyanate ion (\(\mathrm{SCN^{-}}\)) has two distinct potential donor atoms, namely sulfur and nitrogen (\(\mathrm{-SCN}\) or \(\mathrm{-NCS}\)), but binds through only one donor atom at a time to a given metal ion, making it an ambidentate unidentate ligand.

Step 5: Denticity of ammonia
Ammonia (\(\mathrm{NH_{3}}\)) is an uncharged molecule possessing a single lone pair of electrons on its nitrogen atom, functioning as a neutral unidentate ligand.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
The correct correspondence is: \(\mathrm{EDTA^{4-}}\) matches hexadentate chelating ligand; ethane-1,2-diamine matches didentate chelating ligand; \(\mathrm{SCN^{-}}\) matches ambidentate unidentate ligand; and \(\mathrm{NH_{3}}\) matches neutral unidentate ligand.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATION_COMPOUNDS_MATCH_Q06 - Hybridisation and magnetic property of coordination entities

questiontext.text:
Match the complex ions in Column I with their hybridisation and magnetic nature according to Valence Bond Theory in Column II:

Column IColumn II
A. \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_{3})_{6}]^{3+}}\)i. \(sp^3\), paramagnetic
B. \(\mathrm{[CoF_{6}]^{3-}}\)ii. \(dsp^2\), diamagnetic
C. \(\mathrm{[Ni(CN)_{4}]^{2-}}\)iii. \(sp^3d^2\), paramagnetic
D. \(\mathrm{[NiCl_{4}]^{2-}}\)iv. \(d^2sp^3\), diamagnetic

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Valence bond analysis of hexaamminecobalt(III)
Cobalt has an oxidation state of \(+3\) (\(3d^6\)). In the presence of \(\mathrm{NH_{3}}\), electron pairing occurs within the \(3d\) subshell, completely pairing all six electrons into three \(3d\) orbitals. Two empty \(3d\) orbitals along with one \(4s\) and three \(4p\) orbitals undergo \(d^2sp^3\) hybridisation. With zero unpaired electrons, the inner orbital complex is diamagnetic.

Step 2: Valence bond analysis of hexafluoridocobaltate(III)
Cobalt has an oxidation state of \(+3\) (\(3d^6\)). Fluoride is a weak field ligand and does not force pairing of the \(3d\) electrons, leaving four unpaired electrons. Hybridisation uses one \(4s\), three \(4p\), and two outer \(4d\) orbitals, producing \(sp^3d^2\) hybridisation. The outer orbital complex is paramagnetic.

Step 3: Valence bond analysis of tetracyanidonickelate(II)
Nickel has an oxidation state of \(+2\) (\(3d^8\)). Cyanide is a strong field ligand that forces pairing of the two unpaired \(3d\) electrons into a single orbital, leaving one inner \(3d\) orbital vacant. This vacant \(3d\) orbital combines with the \(4s\) and two \(4p\) orbitals to undergo \(dsp^2\) hybridisation, yielding a square planar, diamagnetic complex.

Step 4: Valence bond analysis of tetrachloridonickelate(II)
Nickel has an oxidation state of \(+2\) (\(3d^8\)). Chloride is a weak field ligand and cannot cause electron pairing in the \(3d\) orbitals, leaving two unpaired electrons. The complex undergoes \(sp^3\) hybridisation involving one \(4s\) and three \(4p\) orbitals, forming a tetrahedral, paramagnetic complex.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The correct correspondence is: \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_{3})_{6}]^{3+}}\) matches \(d^2sp^3\), diamagnetic; \(\mathrm{[CoF_{6}]^{3-}}\) matches \(sp^3d^2\), paramagnetic; \(\mathrm{[Ni(CN)_{4}]^{2-}}\) matches \(dsp^2\), diamagnetic; and \(\mathrm{[NiCl_{4}]^{2-}}\) matches \(sp^3\), paramagnetic.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATION_COMPOUNDS_MATCH_Q07 - Industrial and analytical applications of coordination entities

questiontext.text:
Match the reagent/complex in Column I with its specific application in Column II:

Column IColumn II
A. Wilkinson catalyst, \(\mathrm{[(Ph_{3}P)_{3}RhCl]}\)i. Estimation of hardness of water
B. \(\mathrm{Na_{2}EDTA}\)ii. Extraction of gold and silver
C. Cyanide ion, \(\mathrm{CN^{-}}\)iii. Hydrogenation of alkenes
D. Sodium thiosulphate (Hypo)iv. Dissolving unreacted \(\mathrm{AgBr}\) in photography

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Industrial and laboratory roles of complexes
Coordination compounds find extensive application as catalysts, chelating reagents for analytical estimations, complexing agents in hydrometallurgical extractions, and fixing agents in photography.

Step 2: Role of Wilkinson catalyst
The rhodium complex chloridotris(triphenylphosphine)rhodium(I), known as Wilkinson catalyst \(\mathrm{[(Ph_{3}P)_{3}RhCl]}\), is used as a homogeneous catalyst for the hydrogenation of alkenes.

Step 3: Role of disodium EDTA
The disodium salt of ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (\(\mathrm{Na_{2}EDTA}\)) forms stable chelate complexes selectively with \(\mathrm{Ca^{2+}}\) and \(\mathrm{Mg^{2+}}\) ions, enabling the precise estimation and volumetric titration of the hardness of water.

Step 4: Role of cyanide in extraction
In the extraction and metallurgy of noble metals like gold and silver, the crushed ore is leached in the presence of air using an aqueous cyanide solution, forming soluble coordination entities such as \(\mathrm{[Au(CN)_{2}]^{-}}\) and \(\mathrm{[Ag(CN)_{2}]^{-}}\).

Step 5: Role of hypo in black-and-white photography
During the fixing stage of photographic film processing, sodium thiosulphate solution acts as a complexing agent to dissolve unreacted, light-sensitive silver bromide by forming the soluble complex \(\mathrm{[Ag(S_{2}O_{3})_{2}]^{3-}}\).

Step 6: Final Conclusion
The correct correspondence is: Wilkinson catalyst matches hydrogenation of alkenes; \(\mathrm{Na_{2}EDTA}\) matches estimation of hardness of water; cyanide ion matches extraction of gold and silver; and sodium thiosulphate matches dissolving unreacted \(\mathrm{AgBr}\) in photography.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATION_COMPOUNDS_MATCH_Q08 - Absorbed and observed complementary colours in complexes

questiontext.text:
Match the coordination entities in Column I with the colour of light absorbed and their observed complementary colour in Column II:

Column IColumn II
A. \(\mathrm{[Ti(H_{2}O)_{6}]^{3+}}\)i. Absorbs yellow light; observed colour is violet
B. \(\mathrm{[Cu(H_{2}O)_{4}]^{2+}}\)ii. Absorbs blue-green light; observed colour is purple / violet
C. \(\mathrm{[CoCl(NH_{3})_{5}]^{2+}}\)iii. Absorbs blue light; observed colour is yellow-orange
D. \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_{3})_{6}]^{3+}}\)iv. Absorbs red light; observed colour is blue

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Crystal field theory and complementary colours
When white light falls on a transition metal complex, electrons are promoted from the \(t_{2g}\) level to the \(e_g\) level by absorbing radiation of a specific wavelength corresponding to the crystal field splitting energy (\(\Delta_o\)). The colour observed is the complementary colour of the light absorbed.

Step 2: Analysis of hexaaquatitanium(III)
In \(\mathrm{[Ti(H_{2}O)_{6}]^{3+}}\), a \(d^1\) system, excitation of the single electron from the \(t_{2g}\) set to the \(e_g\) set corresponds to absorption of blue-green light (\(498\text{ nm}\)). The observed complementary colour of the complex is purple / violet.

Step 3: Analysis of tetraaquacopper(II)
In \(\mathrm{[Cu(H_{2}O)_{4}]^{2+}}\), the absorption occurs in the red wavelength region (\(600\text{ nm}\)), resulting in the characteristic observed blue colour of the solution.

Step 4: Analysis of pentaamminechloridocobalt(III)
In \(\mathrm{[CoCl(NH_{3})_{5}]^{2+}}\), substitution of an ammine ligand with a weaker-field chloride reduces \(\Delta_o\), shifting absorption to the yellow region (\(535\text{ nm}\)). Consequently, the complex transmits the complementary violet colour.

Step 5: Analysis of hexaamminecobalt(III)
In \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_{3})_{6}]^{3+}}\), the presence of six strong-field ammine ligands produces a larger splitting \(\Delta_o\), causing the complex to absorb higher-energy blue light (\(475\text{ nm}\)). The complementary colour observed is yellow-orange.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
The correct correspondence is: \(\mathrm{[Ti(H_{2}O)_{6}]^{3+}}\) absorbs blue-green and appears purple/violet; \(\mathrm{[Cu(H_{2}O)_{4}]^{2+}}\) absorbs red and appears blue; \(\mathrm{[CoCl(NH_{3})_{5}]^{2+}}\) absorbs yellow and appears violet; and \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_{3})_{6}]^{3+}}\) absorbs blue and appears yellow-orange.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATION_COMPOUNDS_MATCH_Q09 - Unpaired electrons and spin only magnetic moments

questiontext.text:
Match the complex ions in Column I with their number of unpaired electrons and spin-only magnetic moment (\(\mu_{\mathrm{s}}\)) in Column II:

Column IColumn II
A. \(\mathrm{[Mn(CN)_{6}]^{3-}}\)i. \(5\text{ unpaired electrons, }\mu_{\mathrm{s}} = 5.92\text{ BM}\)
B. \(\mathrm{[MnCl_{6}]^{3-}}\)ii. \(1\text{ unpaired electron, }\mu_{\mathrm{s}} = 1.73\text{ BM}\)
C. \(\mathrm{[FeF_{6}]^{3-}}\)iii. \(2\text{ unpaired electrons, }\mu_{\mathrm{s}} = 2.83\text{ BM}\)
D. \(\mathrm{[Fe(CN)_{6}]^{3-}}\)iv. \(4\text{ unpaired electrons, }\mu_{\mathrm{s}} = 4.90\text{ BM}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Formula for spin-only magnetic moment
The spin-only magnetic moment is given by \(\mu_{\mathrm{s}} = \sqrt{n(n+2)}\text{ BM}\), where \(n\) is the number of unpaired electrons in the complex entity.

Step 2: Electronic configuration of hexacyanidomanganate(III)
Manganese is in the \(+3\) oxidation state with a \(3d^4\) electronic configuration. Cyanide is a strong field ligand (\(\Delta_o > P\)), causing pairing in the \(t_{2g}\) set. The configuration is \(t_{2g}^4 e_g^0\), giving \(n = 2\) unpaired electrons. Its magnetic moment is \(\mu_{\mathrm{s}} = \sqrt{2(2+2)} = \sqrt{8} \approx 2.83\text{ BM}\).

Step 3: Electronic configuration of hexachloridomanganate(III)
Manganese is in the \(+3\) oxidation state with a \(3d^4\) configuration. Chloride is a weak field ligand (\(\Delta_o < P\)), giving a high-spin distribution of \(t_{2g}^3 e_g^1\) with \(n = 4\) unpaired electrons. Its magnetic moment is \(\mu_{\mathrm{s}} = \sqrt{4(4+2)} = \sqrt{24} \approx 4.90\text{ BM}\).

Step 4: Electronic configuration of hexafluoridoferrate(III)
Iron is in the \(+3\) oxidation state with a \(3d^5\) configuration. Fluoride is a weak field ligand (\(\Delta_o < P\)), yielding a high-spin configuration of \(t_{2g}^3 e_g^2\) with \(n = 5\) unpaired electrons. Its magnetic moment is \(\mu_{\mathrm{s}} = \sqrt{5(5+2)} = \sqrt{35} \approx 5.92\text{ BM}\).

Step 5: Electronic configuration of hexacyanidoferrate(III)
Iron is in the \(+3\) oxidation state with a \(3d^5\) configuration. Cyanide is a strong field ligand (\(\Delta_o > P\)), driving complete pairing in the \(t_{2g}\) level to produce \(t_{2g}^5 e_g^0\), which contains \(n = 1\) unpaired electron. Its magnetic moment is \(\mu_{\mathrm{s}} = \sqrt{1(1+2)} = \sqrt{3} \approx 1.73\text{ BM}\).

Step 6: Final Conclusion
The correct correspondence is: \(\mathrm{[Mn(CN)_{6}]^{3-}}\) has \(2\) unpaired electrons (\(2.83\text{ BM}\)); \(\mathrm{[MnCl_{6}]^{3-}}\) has \(4\) unpaired electrons (\(4.90\text{ BM}\)); \(\mathrm{[FeF_{6}]^{3-}}\) has \(5\) unpaired electrons (\(5.92\text{ BM}\)); and \(\mathrm{[Fe(CN)_{6}]^{3-}}\) has \(1\) unpaired electron (\(1.73\text{ BM}\)).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATION_COMPOUNDS_MATCH_Q10 - Metal carbonyl structures and oxidation states

questiontext.text:
Match the homoleptic metal carbonyls in Column I with their structural description and features in Column II:

Column IColumn II
A. \(\mathrm{[Ni(CO)_{4}]}\)i. Octahedral geometry with central metal in zero oxidation state
B. \(\mathrm{[Fe(CO)_{5}]}\)ii. Two square pyramidal units joined by a metal-metal bond
C. \(\mathrm{[Cr(CO)_{6}]}\)iii. Tetrahedral geometry with central metal in zero oxidation state
D. \(\mathrm{[Mn_{2}(CO)_{10}]}\)iv. Trigonal bipyramidal geometry with central metal in zero oxidation state

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Principles of metal carbonyl structures and bonding
Homoleptic metal carbonyls are complexes containing only carbon monoxide ligands coordinated to transition metals in zero oxidation states. The metal-carbon bond possesses both \(\sigma\) donation from carbonyl carbon to metal and \(\pi\) back-bonding from filled metal \(d\) orbitals to empty \(\pi^*\) orbitals of \(\mathrm{CO}\).

Step 2: Analysis of tetracarbonylnickel(0)
Tetracarbonylnickel(0), \(\mathrm{[Ni(CO)_{4}]}\), has a nickel atom in the zero oxidation state surrounded symmetrically by four carbonyl ligands in a tetrahedral geometry.

Step 3: Analysis of pentacarbonyliron(0)
Pentacarbonyliron(0), \(\mathrm{[Fe(CO)_{5}]}\), contains iron in the zero oxidation state coordinated to five carbonyl groups positioned at the vertices of a trigonal bipyramid.

Step 4: Analysis of hexacarbonylchromium(0)
Hexacarbonylchromium(0), \(\mathrm{[Cr(CO)_{6}]}\), features a chromium atom in the zero oxidation state coordinated to six carbonyl groups arranged in an octahedral geometry.

Step 5: Analysis of decacarbonyldimanganese(0)
Decacarbonyldimanganese(0), \(\mathrm{[Mn_{2}(CO)_{10}]}\), is a dinuclear neutral carbonyl composed of two square pyramidal \(\mathrm{Mn(CO)_{5}}\) units joined together by a single manganese-manganese (\(\mathrm{Mn-Mn}\)) covalent bond without any bridging carbonyl groups.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
The correct correspondence is: \(\mathrm{[Ni(CO)_{4}]}\) has a tetrahedral geometry with zero oxidation state; \(\mathrm{[Fe(CO)_{5}]}\) has a trigonal bipyramidal geometry with zero oxidation state; \(\mathrm{[Cr(CO)_{6}]}\) has an octahedral geometry with zero oxidation state; and \(\mathrm{[Mn_{2}(CO)_{10}]}\) consists of two square pyramidal units joined by a metal-metal bond.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_NUM_Q01 - Moles of silver chloride precipitated by hexamminecobalt

questiontext.text: When one mole of cobalt(III) chloride hexammine, \(\mathrm{CoCl}_{3}\cdot 6\mathrm{NH}_{3}\), reacts with an excess of silver nitrate solution, how many moles of \(\mathrm{AgCl}\) are precipitated?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Compound formula: \(\mathrm{CoCl}_{3}\cdot 6\mathrm{NH}_{3}\).
Reagent: Excess \(\mathrm{AgNO}_{3}\) solution in cold.
Quantity of complex: \(1\text{ mol}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Chemical Principles
According to Werner's coordination theory, cobalt(III) exhibits a fixed secondary valence (coordination number) of 6. Only the ionisable chloride ions located outside the coordination sphere precipitate as silver chloride upon the addition of silver nitrate.

Step 3: Formulation of the Complex Entity
All six ammonia molecules satisfy the secondary valencies of cobalt(III), giving the cationic complex \([\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{6}]^{3+}\). The three chloride ions satisfy the primary valence and reside in the outer sphere as counter ions: \([\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{6}]\mathrm{Cl}_{3}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Ionisation and Reaction
In aqueous solution, the complex dissociates as:
\[[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{6}]\mathrm{Cl}_{3}\mathrm{(aq)} \rightarrow [\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{6}]^{3+}\mathrm{(aq)} + 3\mathrm{Cl}^{-}\mathrm{(aq)}\]
Reaction with excess silver nitrate:
\[3\mathrm{Cl}^{-}\mathrm{(aq)} + 3\mathrm{Ag}^{+}\mathrm{(aq)} \rightarrow 3\mathrm{AgCl}\mathrm{(s)}\]
Therefore, \(1\text{ mol}\) of \([\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{6}]\mathrm{Cl}_{3}\) yields \(3\text{ moles}\) of \(\mathrm{AgCl}\).

Step 5: Final Check
The primary valence equals 3, all 3 chloride ions are outside the brackets and ionisable, matching the classical precipitation value of 3 moles.

Therefore, the correct answer is 3.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_NUM_Q02 - Total ions produced per formula unit of potassium ferrocyanide

questiontext.text: Find the total number of ions produced in aqueous solution per formula unit of potassium hexacyanidoferrate(II), \(\mathrm{K}_{4}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]\).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Complex compound: \(\mathrm{K}_{4}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]\).
Property required: Total number of ions yielded in solution per formula unit.

Step 2: Principles of Coordination Compounds in Solution
A coordination compound retains its identity in aqueous solution. The species inside the square brackets, \([\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]^{4-}\), acts as a single entity (complex ion) and does not dissociate further into individual iron and cyanide ions. The species outside the brackets are ionisable counter ions.

Step 3: Ionisation Equation
The dissolution of \(\mathrm{K}_{4}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]\) in water produces potassium cations and the complex anion:
\[\mathrm{K}_{4}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]\mathrm{(s)} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}} 4\mathrm{K}^{+}\mathrm{(aq)} + [\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]^{4-}\mathrm{(aq)}\]

Step 4: Counting the Ions
Number of potassium ions (\(\mathrm{K}^{+}\)) = \(4\).
Number of hexacyanidoferrate(II) ions (\([\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]^{4-}\)) = \(1\).
Total ions = \(4 + 1 = 5\).

Step 5: Final Check
The complex behaves as a 1:4 electrolyte, producing a total of 5 ions per formula unit.

Therefore, the correct answer is 5.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_NUM_Q03 - Denticity of the ethylenediaminetetraacetate hexadentate ligand

questiontext.text: What is the denticity (total number of donor atoms) of the ethylenediaminetetraacetate ion, \([\mathrm{EDTA}]^{4-}\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Ligand: Ethylenediaminetetraacetate ion, \([\mathrm{EDTA}]^{4-}\).
Property required: Denticity of the ligand.

Step 2: Definition of Denticity
Denticity refers to the number of donor atoms through which a single ligand is bound to the central metal ion in a coordination entity.

Step 3: Structure and Donor Atoms
The chemical structure of \([\mathrm{EDTA}]^{4-}\) contains two tertiary nitrogen atoms and four acetate carboxylate groups:\((\mathrm{^{-}OOC}-\mathrm{CH}_{2})_{2}\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{N}(\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{COO}^{-})_{2}\).
- The two nitrogen atoms act as donor sites via their lone pairs.
- The four oxygen atoms from the four carboxylate groups act as donor sites.

Step 4: Calculation of Denticity
Total number of donor atoms = \(2\text{ (nitrogen)} + 4\text{ (oxygen)} = 6\). Thus, \([\mathrm{EDTA}]^{4-}\) is a hexadentate ligand.

Step 5: Final Check
Because \([\mathrm{EDTA}]^{4-}\) binds using six coordination sites simultaneously to enclose a metal ion, its denticity is 6.

Therefore, the correct answer is 6.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_NUM_Q04 - Oxidation state of nickel in tetracarbonylnickel complex

questiontext.text: Determine the oxidation state of nickel in the homoleptic metal carbonyl complex \([\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO})_{4}]\).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Complex: \([\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO})_{4}]\).
Central metal: Nickel (\(\mathrm{Ni}\)).
Ligand: Carbon monoxide (carbonyl, \(\mathrm{CO}\)).
Overall charge on the complex: \(0\).

Step 2: Charge of Ligand
Carbon monoxide (\(\mathrm{CO}\)) is a neutral ligand, having a net electrical charge of \(0\).

Step 3: Equation for Oxidation State
Let the oxidation state of nickel be \(x\).
The sum of oxidation states of the central atom and all ligands equals the overall charge on the coordination entity:
\[x + 4(0) = 0\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Solving
\[x + 0 = 0 \implies x = 0\]

Step 5: Final Check
In homoleptic neutral metal carbonyls, the transition metal resides in the zero oxidation state.

Therefore, the correct answer is 0.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_NUM_Q05 - Precipitation of silver chloride from pentamminecobalt chloride

questiontext.text: How many moles of \(\mathrm{AgCl}\) are precipitated when one mole of \(\mathrm{CoCl}_{3}\cdot 5\mathrm{NH}_{3}\) is treated with excess aqueous \(\mathrm{AgNO}_{3}\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Compound: \(\mathrm{CoCl}_{3}\cdot 5\mathrm{NH}_{3}\).
Reagent: Excess aqueous \(\mathrm{AgNO}_{3}\).
Amount of complex: \(1\text{ mol}\).

Step 2: Coordination Principles
Cobalt(III) maintains a coordination number (secondary valence) of 6. Only the chloride ions that are not coordinated directly to the central metal ion exist in the outer sphere and can be precipitated as \(\mathrm{AgCl}\).

Step 3: Formulation of the Complex
To satisfy the coordination number of 6, all five ammonia molecules and one chloride ion reside in the coordination sphere. The remaining two chloride ions act as counter ions outside the coordination entity:
\[[\mathrm{CoCl}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{5}]\mathrm{Cl}_{2}\]

Step 4: Dissociation and Precipitation
In aqueous solution:
\[[\mathrm{CoCl}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{5}]\mathrm{Cl}_{2}\mathrm{(aq)} \rightarrow [\mathrm{CoCl}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{5}]^{2+}\mathrm{(aq)} + 2\mathrm{Cl}^{-}\mathrm{(aq)}\]
Reaction with excess silver ions:
\[2\mathrm{Cl}^{-}\mathrm{(aq)} + 2\mathrm{Ag}^{+}\mathrm{(aq)} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{AgCl}\mathrm{(s)}\]
Thus, \(1\text{ mol}\) of the complex yields \(2\text{ moles}\) of \(\mathrm{AgCl}\).

Step 5: Final Check
Two chloride ions are ionisable, confirming the formation of exactly 2 moles of silver chloride.

Therefore, the correct answer is 2.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_NUM_Q06 - Coordination number of iron in trioxalatoferrate complex

questiontext.text: What is the coordination number of the central iron atom in the complex ion \([\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{C}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4})_{3}]^{3-}\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Complex ion: \([\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{C}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4})_{3}]^{3-}\).
Central metal atom: Iron (\(\mathrm{Fe}\)).
Ligand: Oxalate ion, \(\mathrm{C}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4}^{2-}\).
Number of oxalate ligands = \(3\).

Step 2: Definition and Denticity
The coordination number of a central metal atom/ion in a complex is the total number of ligand donor atoms directly bonded to it. The oxalate ion (\(\mathrm{ox}^{2-}\)) is a didentate (bidentate) ligand, meaning each oxalate ligand provides 2 donor oxygen atoms.

Step 3: Calculation of Coordination Number
\[\text{Coordination Number} = (\text{Number of ligands}) \times (\text{Denticity of each ligand})\]
\[\text{Coordination Number} = 3 \times 2 = 6\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Verification
Three oxalate ligands bind to iron through \(3 \times 2 = 6\) coordinate bonds, forming an octahedral coordination entity.

Step 5: Final Check
The coordination sphere contains 6 metal-ligand coordinate linkages, so the coordination number is 6.

Therefore, the correct answer is 6.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_NUM_Q07 - Oxidation state of copper in tetracyanidocuprate ion

questiontext.text: Calculate the oxidation number of copper in the complex ion \([\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{CN})_{4}]^{3-}\).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Complex entity: \([\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{CN})_{4}]^{3-}\).
Central atom: Copper (\(\mathrm{Cu}\)).
Ligand: Cyanide ion (\(\mathrm{CN}^{-}\))\.
Overall charge on the complex: \(-3\).

Step 2: Charge Contributions
Each cyanide ligand carries a charge of \(-1\). There are 4 cyanide ligands, contributing a total charge of \(4 \times (-1) = -4\).

Step 3: Formulation of Equation
Let the oxidation state of copper be \(x\).
\[x + 4(-1) = -3\]

Step 4: Solving for Oxidation State
\[x - 4 = -3\]
\[x = -3 + 4 = +1\]

Step 5: Final Check
A copper(I) ion with 4 cyanide ions yields a net charge of \(+1 + (-4) = -3\), which matches the given entity charge.

Therefore, the correct answer is 1.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_NUM_Q08 - Number of unpaired electrons in tetrachloridonickelate ion

questiontext.text: Calculate the number of unpaired electrons in the tetrahedral complex ion \([\mathrm{NiCl}_{4}]^{2-}\).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Complex ion: \([\mathrm{NiCl}_{4}]^{2-}\).
Geometry: Tetrahedral.
Central metal: Nickel (\(Z = 28\)).
Ligand: Chloride (\(\mathrm{Cl}^{-}\)), a weak field ligand.

Step 2: Oxidation State and Electron Configuration
Let the oxidation state of nickel be \(x\):
\[x + 4(-1) = -2 \implies x = +2\]
Electronic configuration of neutral \(\mathrm{Ni}\) (\(Z = 28\)): \([\mathrm{Ar}]\,3d^{8}\,4s^{2}\).
Electronic configuration of \(\mathrm{Ni}^{2+}\): \([\mathrm{Ar}]\,3d^{8}\,4s^{0}\).

Step 3: Application of Valence Bond / Crystal Field Theory
Chloride is a weak field ligand, so \(\Delta_{\mathrm{t}} < P\). No pairing of the \(3d\) electrons occurs beyond Hund's rule.
In the \(3d\) subshell containing 8 electrons:
- Three orbitals are fully occupied (paired): \(3 \times 2 = 6\) electrons.
- Two orbitals are singly occupied: \(2\) electrons.
The hybridization is \(sp^{3}\) using the empty \(4s\) and \(4p\) orbitals.

Step 4: Determination of Unpaired Electrons
The number of singly occupied orbitals with unpaired electrons is \(n = 2\).

Step 5: Final Check
The complex is paramagnetic with a magnetic moment corresponding to \(n = 2\) (\(\mu = \sqrt{2(4)} = \sqrt{8} \approx 2.83\text{ BM}\)).

Therefore, the correct answer is 2.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_NUM_Q09 - Unpaired electrons in square planar tetracyanidonickelate ion

questiontext.text: How many unpaired electrons are present in the square planar complex ion \([\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN})_{4}]^{2-}\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Complex ion: \([\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN})_{4}]^{2-}\).
Central metal: Nickel (\(Z = 28\)).
Ligand: Cyanide (\(\mathrm{CN}^{-}\)), a strong field ligand.
Geometry: Square planar.

Step 2: Oxidation State of Nickel
Let the oxidation state of \(\mathrm{Ni}\) be \(x\):
\[x + 4(-1) = -2 \implies x = +2\]
Electron configuration of \(\mathrm{Ni}^{2+}\): \([\mathrm{Ar}]\,3d^{8}\).

Step 3: Valence Bond Analysis
Since cyanide is a strong field ligand, the crystal field splitting is large, forcing electron pairing. The eight \(3d\) electrons pair up completely into four of the \(3d\) orbitals:
\[3d^{8} \rightarrow (\underline{\uparrow\downarrow})\,(\underline{\uparrow\downarrow})\,(\underline{\uparrow\downarrow})\,(\underline{\uparrow\downarrow})\,(\underline{\phantom{\uparrow\downarrow}})\]
This leaves one vacant \(3d\) orbital, which hybridizes with one \(4s\) and two \(4p\) orbitals to form four \(dsp^{2}\) hybrid orbitals directed in a square planar geometry.

Step 4: Counting Unpaired Electrons
All 8 electrons in the \(3d\) level are fully paired. Therefore, the number of unpaired electrons is \(0\).

Step 5: Final Check
The complex is diamagnetic, confirming that the number of unpaired electrons is 0.

Therefore, the correct answer is 0.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_NUM_Q10 - Number of geometrical isomers for square planar platinum complex

questiontext.text: Find the total number of geometrical isomers possible for the square planar coordination entity \([\mathrm{Pt}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})(\mathrm{Br})(\mathrm{Cl})(\mathrm{py})]\).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Coordination complex: \([\mathrm{Pt}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})(\mathrm{Br})(\mathrm{Cl})(\mathrm{py})]\).
Geometry: Square planar.
Central metal: Platinum(II).
Ligands: Four different unidentate ligands: \(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\), \(\mathrm{Br}^{-}\), \(\mathrm{Cl}^{-}\), and pyridine (\(\mathrm{py}\)).

Step 2: General Representation
This complex has the general formulation \([\mathrm{Mabcd}]\), where \(\mathrm{M} = \mathrm{Pt}\) and \(a, b, c, d\) are four distinct unidentate ligands.

Step 3: Step-by-Step Geometric Analysis
In a square planar geometry with positions 1, 2, 3, 4 arranged in order around the metal:
- Fix ligand \(a\) (e.g., \(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\)) at position 1.
- The trans position (position 3) can be occupied by any of the remaining three ligands \(b, c,\) or \(d\):
1. Isomer 1: \(b\) (\(\mathrm{Br}^{-}\)) is trans to \(a\).
2. Isomer 2: \(c\) (\(\mathrm{Cl}^{-}\)) is trans to \(a\).
3. Isomer 3: \(d\) (\(\mathrm{py}\)) is trans to \(a\).
Each choice yields a distinct, non-superimposable geometrical arrangement.

Step 4: Total Number of Geometrical Isomers
The total number of geometrical isomers is \(3\).

Step 5: Final Check
Square planar complexes of type \([\mathrm{Mabcd}]\) always form exactly 3 geometrical isomers.

Therefore, the correct answer is 3.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_NUM_Q11 - Unpaired electrons in low spin hexacyanidoferrate ion

questiontext.text: Determine the number of unpaired electrons in the low-spin octahedral complex ion \([\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]^{3-}\).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Complex ion: \([\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]^{3-}\).
Central metal: Iron (\(Z = 26\)).
Ligand: Cyanide (\(\mathrm{CN}^{-}\)), a strong field ligand.
Type: Low-spin octahedral complex.

Step 2: Oxidation State and d-Electron Count
Let the oxidation state of iron be \(x\):
\[x + 6(-1) = -3 \implies x = +3\]
Neutral \(\mathrm{Fe}\) has the configuration \([\mathrm{Ar}]\,3d^{6}\,4s^{2}\).
\(\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}\) ion has the configuration \([\mathrm{Ar}]\,3d^{5}\).

Step 3: Crystal Field Splitting and Electron Distribution
In an octahedral crystal field, the \(d\) orbitals split into lower energy \(t_{2g}\) and higher energy \(e_{g}\) sets.
Cyanide is a strong field ligand, so the crystal field splitting energy is greater than the pairing energy (\(\Delta_{\mathrm{o}} > P\)), resulting in a low-spin configuration.
All 5 electrons occupy the lower \(t_{2g}\) orbitals with forced pairing:
\[t_{2g}^{5}\,e_{g}^{0}\]

Step 4: Calculation of Unpaired Electrons
The \(t_{2g}\) level accommodates: two pairs of electrons (\(4\) electrons) and one single electron (\(1\) electron).
Therefore, the number of unpaired electrons is \(n = 1\).

Step 5: Final Check
The low-spin \(d^{5}\) configuration \(t_{2g}^{5}\) has exactly 1 unpaired electron, resulting in a spin-only magnetic moment of \(\sqrt{1(3)} = \sqrt{3} \approx 1.73\text{ BM}\).

Therefore, the correct answer is 1.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_NUM_Q12 - Coordination number of iron in pentacarbonyliron complex

questiontext.text: What is the coordination number of the central iron atom in the coordination entity \([\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CO})_{5}]\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Complex: Pentacarbonyliron(0), \([\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CO})_{5}]\).
Central metal atom: Iron (\(\mathrm{Fe}\)).
Ligand: Carbon monoxide (\(\mathrm{CO}\)).
Number of ligands = \(5\).

Step 2: Coordination Principles and Denticity
The coordination number is defined as the total number of sigma bonds formed by the central metal atom with the donor atoms of the ligands. The carbonyl ligand (\(\mathrm{CO}\)) acts as a unidentate ligand, donating through its carbon atom.

Step 3: Calculating Coordination Number
\[\text{Coordination Number} = (\text{Number of ligands}) \times (\text{Denticity})\]
\[\text{Coordination Number} = 5 \times 1 = 5\]

Step 4: Geometry Association
The complex adopts a trigonal bipyramidal geometry corresponding to \(dsp^{3}\) hybridization and a coordination number of 5.

Step 5: Final Check
Iron is bonded to 5 carbon atoms, confirming a coordination number of 5.

Therefore, the correct answer is 5.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_NUM_Q13 - Secondary valence of platinum in non precipitating chloride complex

questiontext.text: When one mole of \(\mathrm{PtCl}_{4}\cdot 2\mathrm{HCl}\) is treated with excess \(\mathrm{AgNO}_{3}\), zero moles of \(\mathrm{AgCl}\) are precipitated. What is the secondary valence (coordination number) of platinum in this compound?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Empirical formula: \(\mathrm{PtCl}_{4}\cdot 2\mathrm{HCl}\).
Precipitate obtained with excess \(\mathrm{AgNO}_{3}\): \(0\text{ moles of }\mathrm{AgCl}\).
Property required: Secondary valence of platinum.

Step 2: Werner's Coordination Theory Principles
Precipitation of zero moles of \(\mathrm{AgCl}\) indicates that none of the chloride ions are present outside the coordination sphere as counter ions. Therefore, all chloride ions are directly coordinated to the central platinum ion, satisfying its secondary valency inside the coordination entity.

Step 3: Formulation of the Complex
The formula contains a total of \(4 + 2 = 6\) chlorine atoms and \(2\) hydrogen atoms. Since all 6 chloride ions are non-ionisable (within the coordination entity), the complex is formulated as:
\[\mathrm{H}_{2}[\mathrm{PtCl}_{6}]\]
Here, \(\mathrm{H}^{+}\) ions are the counter cations, and \([\mathrm{PtCl}_{6}]^{2-}\) is the coordination entity.

Step 4: Determination of Secondary Valence
The secondary valence equals the number of donor atoms bound directly to platinum. In \([\mathrm{PtCl}_{6}]^{2-}\), six chloride ligands are directly bonded to the central platinum(IV) ion.

Step 5: Final Check
The coordination entity has 6 Pt-Cl coordinate bonds, confirming that the secondary valence is 6.

Therefore, the correct answer is 6.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_NUM_Q14 - Number of ions produced by chloridopentamminecobalt chloride

questiontext.text: How many total ions are formed per formula unit when \([\mathrm{CoCl}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{5}]\mathrm{Cl}_{2}\) dissolves completely in water?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Compound: \([\mathrm{CoCl}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{5}]\mathrm{Cl}_{2}\).
Process: Complete dissolution and ionisation in water.

Step 2: Dissociation Behavior of Coordination Compounds
The coordination entity within the square brackets remains intact during dissolution. Only the counter ions located outside the brackets ionise.

Step 3: Ionisation Equation
\[[\mathrm{CoCl}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{5}]\mathrm{Cl}_{2}\mathrm{(aq)} \rightarrow [\mathrm{CoCl}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{5}]^{2+}\mathrm{(aq)} + 2\mathrm{Cl}^{-}\mathrm{(aq)}\]

Step 4: Counting the Dissociated Ions
- Cation: \(1\) complex ion \([\mathrm{CoCl}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{5}]^{2+}\).
- Anions: \(2\) chloride ions \(\mathrm{Cl}^{-}\).
Total number of ions = \(1 + 2 = 3\).

Step 5: Final Check
The complex behaves as a 1:2 electrolyte in aqueous solution, yielding a total of 3 ions per formula unit.

Therefore, the correct answer is 3.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_NUM_Q15 - Unpaired electrons in hexafluoridocobaltate high spin complex

questiontext.text: Calculate the number of unpaired electrons in the octahedral complex ion \([\mathrm{CoF}_{6}]^{3-}\).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Complex entity: \([\mathrm{CoF}_{6}]^{3-}\).
Central metal: Cobalt (\(Z = 27\)).
Ligand: Fluoride (\(\mathrm{F}^{-}\)), a weak field ligand.
Geometry: Octahedral.

Step 2: Oxidation State of Cobalt
Let the oxidation state of cobalt be \(x\):
\[x + 6(-1) = -3 \implies x = +3\]
Ground-state electronic configuration of neutral \(\mathrm{Co}\): \([\mathrm{Ar}]\,3d^{7}\,4s^{2}\).
Electronic configuration of \(\mathrm{Co}^{3+}\): \([\mathrm{Ar}]\,3d^{6}\,4s^{0}\).

Step 3: Crystal Field Splitting and Electron Configuration
In an octahedral crystal field, the \(d\) orbitals split into \(t_{2g}\) and \(e_{g}\) sub-levels.
Because fluoride is a weak field ligand, the crystal field splitting energy is less than the electron pairing energy (\(\Delta_{\mathrm{o}} < P\)).
According to Hund's rule, the 6 electrons occupy orbitals singly before pairing:
- Electrons 1, 2, 3 enter the \(t_{2g}\) orbitals singly.
- Electrons 4, 5 enter the \(e_{g}\) orbitals singly.
- Electron 6 pairs up in one of the \(t_{2g}\) orbitals.
Configuration: \(t_{2g}^{4}\,e_{g}^{2}\).

Step 4: Counting Unpaired Electrons
In \(t_{2g}^{4}\), there is one paired orbital and two singly occupied orbitals (2 unpaired electrons).
In \(e_{g}^{2}\), there are two singly occupied orbitals (2 unpaired electrons).
Total number of unpaired electrons \(n = 2 + 2 = 4\).

Step 5: Final Check
The complex is an outer-orbital high-spin complex (\(sp^{3}d^{2}\)) with 4 unpaired electrons.

Therefore, the correct answer is 4.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_NUM_Q16 - Number of unpaired electrons in tetracyanidoplatinate ion

questiontext.text: Calculate the number of unpaired electrons in the square planar complex ion \([\mathrm{Pt}(\mathrm{CN})_{4}]^{2-}\).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Complex: \([\mathrm{Pt}(\mathrm{CN})_{4}]^{2-}\).
Central metal: Platinum (\(Z = 78\)), a \(5d\) transition metal.
Ligand: Cyanide (\(\mathrm{CN}^{-}\)).
Geometry: Square planar.

Step 2: Oxidation State and Electron Configuration
Let the oxidation state of platinum be \(x\):
\[x + 4(-1) = -2 \implies x = +2\]
\(\mathrm{Pt}^{2+}\) has an electronic configuration of \([\mathrm{Xe}]\,4f^{14}\,5d^{8}\).

Step 3: Crystal Field and Relativistic Effects in 5d Series
For second- and third-row transition elements (such as \(4d\) and \(5d\)), the crystal field splitting parameter \(\Delta\) is very large (approximately 50% larger than in \(3d\) series), which far exceeds the pairing energy \(P\). Consequently, virtually all four-coordinate \(d^{8}\) complexes of platinum(II) adopt a low-spin square planar geometry involving \(dsp^{2}\) hybridization.

Step 4: Electron Configuration and Pairing
Under the square planar crystal field, the eight \(5d\) electrons pair up completely in the four lowest-energy orbitals (\(d_{xz}, d_{yz}, d_{z^2}, d_{xy}\)), leaving the highest-energy \(d_{x^2-y^2}\) orbital empty to participate in \(dsp^{2}\) hybridization.
Because all 8 electrons are fully paired, the number of unpaired electrons is \(0\).

Step 5: Final Check
The complex is diamagnetic, confirming 0 unpaired electrons.

Therefore, the correct answer is 0.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_NUM_Q17 - Difference in unpaired electrons between hexachlorido and hexacyanido manganate

questiontext.text: Calculate the absolute difference in the number of unpaired electrons between the high-spin complex ion \([\mathrm{MnCl}_{6}]^{3-}\) and the low-spin complex ion \([\mathrm{Mn}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]^{3-}\).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Two complex entities: \([\mathrm{MnCl}_{6}]^{3-}\) and \([\mathrm{Mn}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]^{3-}\).
Central metal: Manganese (\(Z = 25\)).
Target: Difference in the number of unpaired electrons between the two complexes.

Step 2: Oxidation State and d-Electron Count
For \([\mathrm{MnCl}_{6}]^{3-}\): \(x + 6(-1) = -3 \implies x = +3\).
For \([\mathrm{Mn}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]^{3-}\): \(x + 6(-1) = -3 \implies x = +3\).
Electronic configuration of \(\mathrm{Mn}\) is \([\mathrm{Ar}]\,3d^{5}\,4s^{2}\).
Electronic configuration of \(\mathrm{Mn}^{3+}\) is \([\mathrm{Ar}]\,3d^{4}\).

Step 3: Crystal Field Analysis for High-Spin Complex
In \([\mathrm{MnCl}_{6}]^{3-}\), \(\mathrm{Cl}^{-}\) is a weak field ligand (\(\Delta_{\mathrm{o}} < P\)), producing a high-spin configuration.
The four \(3d\) electrons occupy orbitals singly according to Hund's rule: \(t_{2g}^{3}\,e_{g}^{1}\).
Number of unpaired electrons \(n_{1} = 3 + 1 = 4\).

Step 4: Crystal Field Analysis for Low-Spin Complex
In \([\mathrm{Mn}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]^{3-}\), \(\mathrm{CN}^{-}\) is a strong field ligand (\(\Delta_{\mathrm{o}} > P\)), producing a low-spin configuration.
All four electrons enter the lower \(t_{2g}\) orbitals: \(t_{2g}^{4}\,e_{g}^{0}\).
In \(t_{2g}^{4}\), one orbital is paired (2 electrons) and two orbitals are singly occupied (2 electrons).
Number of unpaired electrons \(n_{2} = 2\).

Step 5: Calculation and Final Check
Absolute difference = \(|n_{1} - n_{2}| = 4 - 2 = 2\).

Therefore, the correct answer is 2.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_NUM_Q18 - Total donor nitrogen atoms in the ligand tren

questiontext.text: What is the total number of nitrogen donor atoms available for coordination in a single molecule of the tetradentate ligand \(\mathrm{N}(\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{NH}_{2})_{3}\) (tris(2-aminoethyl)amine)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Ligand: \(\mathrm{N}(\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{NH}_{2})_{3}\), commonly abbreviated as tren (tris(2-aminoethyl)amine).
Target: Total number of nitrogen donor atoms coordinating to a central metal ion.

Step 2: Molecular Structure Analysis
The molecule features a central tertiary nitrogen atom bonded to three 2-aminoethyl arms: \(-\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{NH}_{2}\).
- The central tertiary amino group: \(1\) nitrogen atom possessing a lone pair.
- The three terminal primary amino groups: \(3\) nitrogen atoms, each possessing a lone pair.

Step 3: Denticity and Coordination Capacity
Each of the four nitrogen atoms has a lone pair of electrons oriented such that all four can coordinate simultaneously to a single central metal atom/ion, forming a tripodal tetradentate chelate ring system.

Step 4: Summation of Donor Atoms
Total donor nitrogen atoms = \(1\text{ (tertiary)} + 3\text{ (primary)} = 4\).

Step 5: Final Check
Because the ligand is tetradentate and coordinates exclusively via its nitrogen atoms, it possesses exactly 4 donor nitrogen atoms.

Therefore, the correct answer is 4.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_NUM_Q19 - Total ions yielded per formula unit of Prussian blue complex

questiontext.text: Calculate the total number of ions produced per formula unit when iron(III) hexacyanidoferrate(II), \(\mathrm{Fe}_{4}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]_{3}\), is dissolved completely in water.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Compound: Iron(III) hexacyanidoferrate(II), \(\mathrm{Fe}_{4}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]_{3}\) (Prussian blue).
Process: Complete electrolytic dissociation in aqueous solution.

Step 2: Principles of Coordination Compound Ionisation
The complex entity inside the square bracket, \([\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]^{4-}\), remains intact as a single coordinate ion in aqueous solution, while the outer ions dissociate completely into simple hydrated cations.

Step 3: Dissociation Equation
\[\mathrm{Fe}_{4}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]_{3}\mathrm{(s)} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}} 4\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}\mathrm{(aq)} + 3[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]^{4-}\mathrm{(aq)}\]

Step 4: Summation of Produced Ions
- Number of iron(III) cations (\(\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}\)) = \(4\).
- Number of hexacyanidoferrate(II) complex anions (\([\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]^{4-}\)) = \(3\).
Total number of ions = \(4 + 3 = 7\).

Step 5: Final Check
Electroneutrality check: Total positive charge = \(4 \times (+3) = +12\); Total negative charge = \(3 \times (-4) = -12\). Net charge is zero. The dissociation yields a total of 7 ions per formula unit.

Therefore, the correct answer is 7.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATIONCOMPOUNDS_NUM_Q20 - Unpaired electrons in weak field octahedral d4 electronic configuration

questiontext.text: For an octahedral complex of a transition metal ion with a \(d^{4}\) configuration, calculate the number of unpaired electrons when the crystal field splitting energy is smaller than the pairing energy (\(\Delta_{\mathrm{o}} < P\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Coordination geometry: Octahedral.
Electronic configuration of the central ion: \(d^{4}\).
Condition: Weak crystal field, \(\Delta_{\mathrm{o}} < P\) (pairing energy exceeds crystal field splitting).

Step 2: Crystal Field Splitting Theory
In an octahedral crystal field, five degenerate \(d\) orbitals split into two sets separated by energy \(\Delta_{\mathrm{o}}\):
- Triply degenerate lower-energy \(t_{2g}\) set (\(d_{xy}, d_{yz}, d_{zx}\)).
- Doubly degenerate higher-energy \(e_{g}\) set (\(d_{x^2-y^2}, d_{z^2}\)).

Step 3: Electron Filling Order
When \(\Delta_{\mathrm{o}} < P\), the energy required to promote an electron into the higher-energy \(e_{g}\) level is less than the energy penalty required to pair two electrons in the same \(t_{2g}\) orbital. Therefore, the complex adopts a high-spin state:
- The first three electrons occupy the three \(t_{2g}\) orbitals singly with parallel spins.
- The fourth electron enters one of the higher-energy \(e_{g}\) orbitals rather than pairing up in a \(t_{2g}\) orbital.
Resulting ground-state electronic configuration: \(t_{2g}^{3}\,e_{g}^{1}\).

Step 4: Determination of Unpaired Electrons
All 4 electrons reside singly in separate orbitals with parallel spins.
Number of unpaired electrons \(n = 4\).

Step 5: Final Check
In the high-spin \(d^{4}\) state (\(t_{2g}^{3}\,e_{g}^{1}\)), there are no paired electrons, confirming exactly 4 unpaired electrons.

Therefore, the correct answer is 4.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATION_COMPOUNDS_SEQ_Q01 - Sequence of molar conductivity in cobalt ammine complexes

questiontext.text:
Consider the following coordination compounds investigated by Alfred Werner:

  1. \(\mathrm{CoCl_3\cdot 6NH_3}\)
  2. \(\mathrm{CoCl_3\cdot 5NH_3}\)
  3. \(\mathrm{CoCl_3\cdot 4NH_3}\)
  4. \(\mathrm{CoCl_3\cdot 3NH_3}\)

Which of the following represents the correct decreasing order of electrical conductivity of their equimolar aqueous solutions?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Werner's formulations and electrolyte types
According to Werner's theory, only ions located outside the coordination sphere dissociate into free mobile ions in aqueous solution, which determine electrical conductivity.

Step 2: Number of ions produced in solution
The complex \(\mathrm{CoCl_3\cdot 6NH_3}\) is formulated as \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]Cl_3}\) and dissociates into 4 ions (\(1:3\) electrolyte: \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}\) and \(3\mathrm{Cl^-}\)).
The complex \(\mathrm{CoCl_3\cdot 5NH_3}\) is formulated as \(\mathrm{[CoCl(NH_3)_5]Cl_2}\) and dissociates into 3 ions (\(1:2\) electrolyte: \(\mathrm{[CoCl(NH_3)_5]^{2+}}\) and \(2\mathrm{Cl^-}\)).
The complex \(\mathrm{CoCl_3\cdot 4NH_3}\) is formulated as \(\mathrm{[CoCl_2(NH_3)_4]Cl}\) and dissociates into 2 ions (\(1:1\) electrolyte: \(\mathrm{[CoCl_2(NH_3)_4]^+}\) and \(\mathrm{Cl^-}\)).
The complex \(\mathrm{CoCl_3\cdot 3NH_3}\) is formulated as \(\mathrm{[CoCl_3(NH_3)_3]}\) and is a non-electrolyte yielding 0 free ions.

Step 3: Determination of the sequence
Because electrical conductivity in equimolar solutions increases with the total number of ions produced per formula unit, the decreasing order of electrical conductivity is: \[ \mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]Cl_3} > \mathrm{[CoCl(NH_3)_5]Cl_2} > \mathrm{[CoCl_2(NH_3)_4]Cl} > \mathrm{[CoCl_3(NH_3)_3]} \]

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The correct sequence corresponds to \(\mathrm{I > II > III > IV}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATION_COMPOUNDS_SEQ_Q02 - Sequence of ligands in spectrochemical series

questiontext.text:
The spectrochemical series arranges ligands in order of increasing crystal field splitting energy (\(\Delta_\mathrm{o}\)). Consider the following four ligands:

  1. \(\mathrm{Br^-}\)
  2. \(\mathrm{F^-}\)
  3. \(\mathrm{H_2O}\)
  4. \(\mathrm{CN^-}\)

Which of the following represents the correct increasing order of their ligand field strength?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Spectrochemical series definition
The spectrochemical series is an experimentally determined sequence based on the absorption spectra of coordination complexes with different ligands, arranging ligands in order of increasing \(\Delta_\mathrm{o}\).

Step 2: Canonical order in the textbook
The NCERT spectrochemical series is: \[ \mathrm{I^- < Br^- < SCN^- < Cl^- < S^{2-} < F^- < OH^- < C_2O_4^{2-} < H_2O < NCS^- < edta^{4-} < NH_3 < en < CN^- < CO} \]

Step 3: Ordering the selected ligands
Extracting the given four ligands: \[ \mathrm{Br^- < F^- < H_2O < CN^-} \]

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The sequence from weakest to strongest ligand field strength is \(\mathrm{I < II < III < IV}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATION_COMPOUNDS_SEQ_Q03 - Chronological sequence of colour changes in nickel ethylenediamine system

questiontext.text:
When the didentate ligand ethane-1,2-diamine (\(\mathrm{en}\)) is progressively added to an aqueous solution containing \(\mathrm{[Ni(H_2O)_6]^{2+}}\) in molar ratios of \(\mathrm{en : Ni}\) equal to \(1:1\), \(2:1\), and \(3:1\), distinct sequential colour changes occur:

  1. Formation of \(\mathrm{[Ni(en)_3]^{2+}(aq)}\)
  2. Formation of \(\mathrm{[Ni(H_2O)_4(en)]^{2+}(aq)}\)
  3. Initial hydrated cation \(\mathrm{[Ni(H_2O)_6]^{2+}(aq)}\)
  4. Formation of \(\mathrm{[Ni(H_2O)_2(en)_2]^{2+}(aq)}\)

What is the correct sequential order of the appearance of these species as \(\mathrm{en}\) is progressively added, and what is the corresponding sequence of observed colours?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Chemical reactions of sequential ligand substitution
When ethane-1,2-diamine is added successively to an aqueous nickel(II) solution: 1. Initially, the hexaaqua ion exists alone: \(\mathrm{[Ni(H_2O)_6]^{2+}}\), which is green. 2. At a molar ratio of \(\mathrm{en : Ni} = 1:1\), two aqua ligands are displaced: \[ \mathrm{[Ni(H_2O)_6]^{2+} + en \rightarrow [Ni(H_2O)_4(en)]^{2+} + 2H_2O} \quad (\text{pale blue}) \] 3. At a molar ratio of \(\mathrm{en : Ni} = 2:1\), another two aqua ligands are displaced: \[ \mathrm{[Ni(H_2O)_4(en)]^{2+} + en \rightarrow [Ni(H_2O)_2(en)_2]^{2+} + 2H_2O} \quad (\text{blue / purple}) \] 4. At a molar ratio of \(\mathrm{en : Ni} = 3:1\), all remaining aqua ligands are displaced: \[ \mathrm{[Ni(H_2O)_2(en)_2]^{2+} + en \rightarrow [Ni(en)_3]^{2+} + 2H_2O} \quad (\text{violet}) \]

Step 2: Species sequence
The sequential chronological appearance of species is \(\mathrm{III \rightarrow II \rightarrow IV \rightarrow I}\).

Step 3: Colour sequence
The corresponding observed colour progression is Green \(\rightarrow\) Pale blue \(\rightarrow\) Blue/Purple \(\rightarrow\) Violet.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The correct sequence of species is \(\mathrm{III \rightarrow II \rightarrow IV \rightarrow I}\) with the progression Green \(\rightarrow\) Pale blue \(\rightarrow\) Blue/Purple \(\rightarrow\) Violet.

answer.text: \(\mathrm{III \rightarrow II \rightarrow IV \rightarrow I}\) (Green \(\rightarrow\) Pale blue \(\rightarrow\) Blue/Purple \(\rightarrow\) Violet)
